plan.planning_summary: Refining route_01 based on prior iteration evidence. Iteration_04 (16-layer periodic) achieved best_target_score=0.865, while iteration_07 (12-layer) achieved 0.761. Feedback directives specify: (1) relax period scaling bounds by ±8% around quarter-wave baseline, (2) switch from deterministic grid initialization to uniform random sampling, (3) add Monte Carlo resampling checkpoint after 4 iterations without improvement. Four complementary routes explore different layer counts (16, 20, 24, 28) within the 30-layer constraint, all using HfO2/SiO2 on fused silica, with expanded thickness bounds and randomized initialization to escape local minima identified in prior runs.

routes.title: 16-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Dual-Band Filter with Expanded Bounds and Random Initialization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with thickness bounds relaxed by ±8% from quarter-wave values and uniform random initialization will escape the local minimum observed in iteration_04, achieving higher dual-band performance through non-quarter-wave optimization.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg reflector principle for UV band (200-400 nm) with non-quarter-wave thickness optimization to maintain SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm). Random initialization prevents convergence to the same local basin as prior deterministic runs.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (16 finite layers, 8 pairs)
design_variables: Thickness bounds: quarter-wave ±8% at 300 nm center UV wavelength
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Minimize spectral ripple in both bands
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 are deposition-compatible via ion-assisted deposition
Outermost SiO2 layer provides environmental durability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for high-reflectance bands
Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: ±8% bounds allow escape from quarter-wave local minimum
Random initialization increases design space exploration
known_risks: May converge to similar local minimum as iteration_04 if bounds too restrictive
16 layers may be insufficient for simultaneous UV reflection and SWIR transmission optimization
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on fused silica substrate for dual-band performance. Layer sequence: HfO2/SiO2 repeated 8 times starting with HfO2 at air interface. Initialize all layer thicknesses with uniform random sampling within bounds: HfO2 layers 38-45 nm, SiO2 layers 47-55 nm (quarter-wave at 300 nm ±8%). Optimize thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with Adam-LBFGS hybrid. Spectral evaluation: 200-1500 nm with 1 nm resolution. Objectives: maximize mean transmittance 800-1500 nm, maximize mean reflectance 200-400 nm. Total layer count fixed at 16. Material registry resolves HfO2 and SiO2 refractive indices. If best_target_score improvement < 1e-3 for 4 consecutive iterations, trigger Monte Carlo resampling of thickness initialization. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Refinement of iteration_04 16-layer design: expanded thickness bounds by ±8%, switched from deterministic grid initialization to uniform random sampling per feedback directives, added Monte Carlo resampling checkpoint to escape local minima.

routes.title: 24-Layer HfO2/SiO2 Dual-Band Filter with Graded Thickness Profile
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer stack with graded thickness profile (thinner inner layers for UV reflection, thicker outer layers for SWIR transmission) will achieve superior dual-band performance compared to uniform periodic structures.
routes.design_principle: Graded-index inspired design where layer thicknesses vary systematically through the stack to create smooth optical impedance transitions, reducing reflection in SWIR band while maintaining UV reflection through inner quarter-wave layers.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (24 finite layers, 12 pairs)

soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band

Minimize spectral oscillations in transition region
manufacturing_considerations: Graded thickness profile requires precise thickness control per layer
SiO2 outermost layer for durability per evidence
theory_basis: Graded-index antireflection principle for broadband transmission
